findings.claim: Removing the `hasFailed` check means collection/parse failures during static parsing no longer set `process.exitCode = 1`, so `vitest list`/collect runs that fail to parse test files will now exit with status 0.
findings.rationale: This is a user-visible behavior change: CI pipelines relying on a non-zero exit code when a test file fails to be statically parsed would now silently pass. If the intent is to move the exit-code handling to the caller, that must be verified; otherwise failures are swallowed. Confidence: moderate-high that this changes exit status for the failure path, lower on whether an equivalent check exists downstream.

findings.claim: Static-parse path and the `collectTests(files)` fallback path may now behave inconsistently with respect to setting the process exit code on failed modules.
findings.rationale: If `collectTests` (or its callers) still marks failures via `process.exitCode`, the two code paths of the same public API return the same shape but yield different exit statuses depending on `options.staticParse`, which is surprising for callers. Confidence: medium — depends on what `collectTests` does internally.

findings.claim: `hasFailed` may now be an unused import in this file, which can break the build under `noUnusedLocals`/lint rules.
findings.rationale: This was possibly the only use of `hasFailed` in core.ts; if so the import must be removed. Confidence: low-medium, since the import may still be used elsewhere in the file (I can only see this hunk).
